intent: Hold the iteration-2 geometry unchanged: five 16 mm sensors at x = -0.05 to +0.05 m, y = 0.04 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 by 0.18 m, mass 0.8 kg. This is the best-scoring row (26.9949), and no tested change has moved max_error off 0.061 m. I expect the same score, roughly 26.99, with zero line loss and max_error near 0.061 m. I am not making a geometry change without a hypothesis. If the Integrator's controller changes the excursion, I will revisit span and sensor placement against the new behaviour.
learning: Eight iterations show that geometry has been explored across span, footprint, y, track, radius and mass. Only span changed line loss, and nothing has moved the 0.061 m excursion. If the controller cannot bring max_error below 0.06 m, no allowed geometry will change the outcome, so the remaining gain is in control. The Integrator should report whether the excursion occurs at the start of the run or at one bend, since a start-up bias and a steady offset need different responses.
rationale: Iteration 8 (wheel_track 0.10 m) scored 26.9949 with max_error 0.0614, 0.0611 and 0.0609, the same as the iteration-2 row. Track width is now tested at 0.10, 0.12 and 0.15 m, and none of them moves the excursion. I took the Integrator's advice to test 0.10 m, and the result settles it. Across iterations 0 to 8, every run ends off_track with max_error about 0.061 m, just above the fixed 0.06 m off-track floor. The floor is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), and the largest allowed body (0.18 m) gives only 0.0575 m, so the floor cannot be raised by geometry. Levers tested with no effect on max_error: footprint (12 vs 16 mm), wheel_track (0.10, 0.12, 0.15 m), mass (0.6 vs 0.8 kg), wheel_radius (0.03 vs 0.04 m; 0.04 m was worse) and sensor y (0.02, 0.04 m same; 0.06 m added line loss). Span ±0.05 m is the only change that mattered, and it removed line loss. I considered a wider span (±0.07 m) and a 7-sensor row. Neither has a supporting hypothesis, since span already removed line loss and span changes did not move max_error. So I hold the best-scoring row (iteration 2 geometry, which scored 26.9949 in iterations 2, 4, 6 and 8) rather than adding an untested change. The remaining excursion looks like a steady bias from the fixed motor mismatch or a start-up transient, which the controller rather than the geometry must absorb. I do not expect a score change from this geometry, and I am asking the Integrator to report where in the run the excursion occurs.
